card.name: Saman
card.era: Roots attributed to 13th century; developed by Syekh Saman
card.tagline: Gayo seated dance of synchronized claps and Islamic verse
card.profile: The Saman is a seated dance of the Gayo people of Aceh province, Sumatra (UNESCO; Wikipedia). Boys and young men kneel in tight rows and clap their hands, slap their chests, thighs and the ground, click their fingers and sway and twist in time with a shifting rhythm, with no musical instruments. The sung verses - in the Gayo language - offer religious, romantic or humorous guidance and were historically a medium of Islamic preaching (dakwah) developed by Syekh Saman. A leader called the syekh directs the movements. Performances cement relationships between villages who invite each other to perform.
card.insight: Saman was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding on 24 November 2011 (6.COM, Bali), with UNESCO noting weakening transmission as knowledgeable elders age without successors (UNESCO; ANTARA).
